name: What is the difference between building condominiums and apartment buildings?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between building condominiums and apartment buildings?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference between condominiums and apartment buildings lies in ownership. In an apartment building, a single entity or owner typically owns all units, which are then leased to tenants. For condominiums, individual units are owned by separate individuals, while common areas like hallways and amenities are co-owned through a homeowners' association. Construction methods can be similar, but legal and financial structures differ significantly, impacting design choices and required amenities.
acceptedAnswer.description: Condominiums involve individual unit ownership, while apartment buildings are typically owned by a single entity that leases units. Ownership structure dictates legal and financial aspects.
